english: I will call you tomorrow.
tip: The verbs звонить (zvonit) and позвонить (pozvonit = to call) take the dative person: позвоню тебе (pozvonyu tebe = I will call you).

english: They used to meet every day.
tip: Imperfective past marks a repeated habit: встречались каждый день (vstrechalis kazhdyy den = used to meet every day).

english: She complains about a headache.
tip: жаловаться на (zhalovatsya na = to complain about) takes the accusative: жалуется на головную боль (zhaluetsya na golovnuyu bol = complains about a headache).

english: We agree with this plan.
tip: с (s = with) takes the instrumental: соглашаемся с планом (soglashaemsya s planom = agree with the plan), from план (plan).

english: They built their house themselves.
tip: In the third person свой (svoy = one's own) keeps it clear: построили свой дом (postroili svoy dom = built their own house).

english: Tall pines grow around the lake.
tip: вокруг (vokrug = around) takes the genitive: вокруг озера (vokrug ozera = around the lake), from озеро (ozero = lake).

target: В деревне свежий воздух и тишина.
english: The village has fresh air and silence.
tip: Russian drops is in the present: В деревне свежий воздух (v derevne svezhiy vozdukh = in the village there is fresh air) has no verb.

english: He is smarter than he seems.
tip: Add -ее for the comparative: умнее (umneye = smarter) from умный (umnyy = smart), then чем (chem = than) for the comparison.

english: The bright sun shines in one's eyes.
tip: в plus the accusative shows motion into: светит в глаза (svetit v glaza = shines into the eyes), direction not location.

english: Fresh fruits are sold at the market.
tip: A they-verb with no subject reads as passive: продают фрукты (prodayut frukty = fruits are sold), literally they sell.

english: The driver drives the bus in the mornings.
tip: по plus the dative plural marks a recurring time: по утрам (po utram = in the mornings), from утро (utro = morning).

english: We will buy groceries.
tip: Perfective verbs make the future in one word, no будем (budem) needed: купим (kupim) already means we will buy.

english: It will rain tomorrow.
tip: For weather and existence, будет (budet) alone means there will be: будет дождь (budet dozhd = there will be rain).

english: We will help mom.
tip: The verb помогать (pomogat = to help) takes the dative, so mom becomes маме (mame), not маму (mamu).

english: He helped me yesterday.
tip: Most masculine past verbs end in the -l sound, but помог (pomog = he helped) drops it entirely.

english: I wrote a letter recently.
tip: The past ending reveals the speaker's gender: написала (napisala) ending in -la means a woman is speaking.

english: Yesterday I found the exercise.
tip: The verb найти (nayti = to find) has an irregular past: нашёл (nashyol = found), where the stem changes completely.

english: I will wait for the bus.
tip: The verb быть (byt = to be) builds the future: буду (budu = I will) plus an imperfective infinitive like ждать (zhdat = to wait).

english: In the morning they made breakfast.
tip: In the morning is just the instrumental used as a time word: Утром (utrom), from утро (utro = morning).

english: Will you have dinner with us?
tip: The word с (s = with) takes the instrumental case, turning we into с нами (s nami = with us).

english: Every day I bought dinner.
tip: For a repeated past action use the imperfective: покупал (pokupal = kept buying) fits каждый день (kazhdyy den = every day).

english: She needs to buy a new coat.
tip: нужно (nuzhno = need) puts the person in the dative: Ей нужно (yey nuzhno = she needs), literally to her it is needed.

english: A glass of water is on the table.
tip: A container plus its contents puts the contents in the genitive: воды (vody = of water), from вода (voda = water).

english: I used to open the window every morning.
tip: The imperfective past also means used to: открывал (otkryval = used to open) matches the habit каждое утро (kazhdoye utro = every morning).

english: This movie is more interesting than the previous one.
tip: интереснее (interesneye = more interesting) is the comparative, and чем (chem = than) introduces what it is compared against.

target: Птицы поют в саду каждое утро.
english: The birds sing in the garden every morning.
tip: A few masculine nouns take a stressed -u in the location form: в саду (v sadu = in the garden), not в саде (v sade).

target: Дедушка гуляет в парке перед завтраком.
english: Grandpa takes a walk in the park before breakfast.
tip: The word перед (pered = before) takes the instrumental: перед завтраком (pered zavtrakom = before breakfast).

target: Медсестра каждый день ездит на работу на автобусе.
english: The nurse commutes to work by bus every day.
tip: By bus is на (na) plus the prepositional case: на автобусе (na avtobuse), the standard way to name transport.

target: Сегодня утром учитель пишет письмо в парке.
english: This morning the teacher is writing a letter in the park.
tip: писать (pisat = to write) shifts to пишет (pishet = writes) in the present, with the s sound becoming sh.

target: Я читал эту книгу, но так и не дочитал.
english: I read this book but never finished it.
tip: читал (chital = was reading) marks the activity with no result, while perfective дочитал (dochital = finished reading) marks completion.
